utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. The accused are all here. Defence teams are all here. And Prosecution I notice apart from Mr. Thayer, Mr. McCloskey, also Mr. Nicholls. Good afternoon to you, Colonel. Welcome back. I'm sorry for the delay in starting with your testimony but this was due to some technical problem related to the transportation of the accused to the Tribunal, over which we had no control. Mr. Thayer, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you and your colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel. We left off yesterday with you marking an overhead view of the UN base and you marked the compound, the bus station, and the factories area. Sir, in your prior testimony, you testified that photographs were taken. Would you please provide the Trial Chamber with a little bit more detail in terms of who took the photographs and what the photographs depicted?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'll do that. The photographs were taken by Lieutenant Rutten. He took various pictures of the nine bodies we found there. And I kneeled between the bodies to show that the UN found the bodies and I appear on one of those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you have reason to believe at some point that you had in fact been seen by VRS soldiers?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was when we wanted to return to report what we had found, and the moment we left the meadow where the bodies were, a Serb soldier suddenly came out of one of the houses and saw us, and immediately put his radio to his head, probably to report about us. He also seemed startled that we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what if anything happened after that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: At that point we decided because we had the feeling that we had been discovered at a site we didn't -- where we didn't want to be seen, we decided to take an alternative route back to the compound so that we didn't walk past the four YPRs where there were a lot of Serb soldiers and we opted for an alternative route and once we had walked less than 30 metres along that, we came under fire and we turned around and returned along the route that we had taken to reach the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you also testified that someone in your group had picked up some papers or documents at the scene. Can you tell the Trial Chamber a little bit more about what those documents were, to your knowledge, and what, if anything, happened to those documents?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: We found the documents near the bodies, Major van Schaik took the documents and kept them as evidence because they were official documents. There were names on them. I couldn't read them. And en route, Major van Schaik, after we had come under fire, he threw out the papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, sir, what happened to the photographs or film that Lieutenant Rutten had taken of you and of the bodies at the scene?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: In the Netherlands, they were handed over to the military information service, and unfortunately, they -- the development was unsuccessful and the images were lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn your attention now for just a few minutes to two or three areas which you did not testify about in your Rule 61 hearing but which are relevant to the purposes for which you have been called to testify today. Specifically I want to ask you a few questions concerning the resupply situation, given your role as logistics officer. Briefly, sir, can you just describe how the requests for resupplies were communicated from DutchBat to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: We filled in an application form, listing the load in a logistics convoy, and that was sent to the higher echelon at the north-east command, and through higher echelons it reached the Bosnian Serb headquarters in Pale and they would grant permission as to whether the logistics convoy was allowed to depart.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were there any items which the VRS categorically denied from even being on the requested list?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. I'm awfully sorry but he was not talking about the headquarters of the Serbs in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In his previous answer, at least according to the transcript, it says, "it reached the Bosnian Serb headquarters in Pale."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this is not the army of Republika Srpska. This is the headquarters of the Serbs in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think she is correct, in that in other words you understand that to be the Bosnian Serb political and governmental headquarters of Republika Srpska, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is easily a question I think can be put to the witness as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, when you referred to the Bosnian Serb headquarters in Pale, what entity did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serb headquarters in Pale were to me a military headquarters. That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if I may, I'm going to just repeat the question I asked you before, sir. Were there items which the VRS categorically denied from even being placed on the requested resupply list?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Once again, these would have been weapons, ammunition, spare parts. They were categorically denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did there come a time, sir, when the resupply convoys became more restricted, in other words arrived or approved less frequently?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Absolutely. For example, at one point, logistics convoys were no longer allowed with fuel, especially diesel fuel. On 18 February for example the full diesel convoy was blocked, when the -- that was the last convoy that entered the enclave. Only in June was another convoy allowed to enter the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, sir, do I understand your testimony correctly that the last convoy that was able to come through was 18 February and that there was not another one to your knowledge until June?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the diesel convoy is concerned, but as for other logistics supplies such as food and medical supplies, we also saw a change there, that they were also reduced and occasionally they were refused. Rations were provided in dribs and drabs and many convoys with fresh food were also rejected.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you remember when that tightening began to occur, sir?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: As I mentioned, the fuel convoys stopped from 18 February onward, and the food convoys were significantly reduced from the start of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to turn your attention to the events following the VRS attack on the enclave and just ask you a few questions in connection with that period of time. First I want to turn your attention to 10 July. You testified that you were assigned to receive an expected influx of refugees. Do you have any particular memories of any injured arriving in that evening of 10 July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. We received a report of an injured woman lying at a certain site. A local resident told us about this when we were outside that evening to receive the refugees. I went along. We had to cross the road, and at that point, the road was regularly under fire so you had to time your crossing carefully, and we found the woman. She was injured. She was lying on a stretcher but we couldn't transport her on that stretcher so we transferred her to our own stretcher and brought the woman to our own compound. Unfortunately I understand that the woman died of her injuries later that week. The injuries looked like injuries from shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention now to 11 July, sir. That afternoon, there was close air support. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where you were at that time?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: During the close air support situation, I was in the bunker at first and at the end of the close air support I went outside with the people assigned to me, and at the end of the close air support, I was near the former bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was your assignment there at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: At that point I was responsible for receiving the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now I want to turn your attention to the morning of 12 July. In your September 1995 statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, that's at page 10 of the English and page 9 of the B/C/S, third paragraph of that version, you said, "On Wednesday, 12 July 1995, I actually expected the Serbs would shell the refugees." Why did you expect the Serbs to shell the refugees at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just a slight, I don't think he read it properly or in full context but I think if he reads the entire sentence it might help a little better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know the exact location from the testimony that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'd be happy to do that, Your Honour. It has to do with the night before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Once it has been contested, I think it will be better if you do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This refers to the evening of the 11th. "At around 2030 hours I returned to the compound. We held consultations with Major Otter and Franken, we then decided to set up four posts around the refugees for the coming night. There were ten men at each post. There was also a patrol on the north side. On Wednesday, 12 July 1995, I actually expected that the Serbs would shell the refugees but fortunately this did not occur. At around 1300 hours I heard on the walkie-talkie that an armoured vehicle and a tank were approaching the compound from the Yellow Bridge."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "I received orders from Major Otter by walkie-talkie not to aim any weapons at these vehicles."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You can now put again your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, again, why did you say that you actually expected that the Serbs would shell the refugees on that morning of 12 July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, the previous evening, we were shelled, when dusk was falling. We were shelled twice. There was a brief period in between. The shells fell in between the houses, about 50 or 75 metres away from the refugees. It happened twice that evening. And that's why I expected that the next morning, more shelling would follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention to some conversations that you had with General Mladic, and you testified about that previously?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Mr. President, I would like to object to the way my colleague is conducting his examination-in-chief. This is absolutely lead -- these are leading questions. He's using previous statements to recall, to remind the witness what he said previously in order to get a confirmation. This is examination-in-chief. He should be asking the question -- the witness open questions so the witness can say what he knows and what he remembers. There are very specific rulings before there Tribunal in terms of if there is a need for using past statements, that's in a -- very specific circumstances that can be allowed. But my right now my colleague is conducting a cross-examination. He should be simply asking the witness what happened on the 11th, what happened on the 12th, what happened in the afternoon? But not to take a statement, remind the witness what he said two years ago, and then say, well, do you recall saying that? I mean if there is a need to do, into the past statements, this will be for the Defence to take this on cross-examination. But not under examination-in-chief. It's both leading and it's not the conduct of a proper examination-in-chief. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will join in the objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour, the whole intention of introducing this testimony via 92 bis is to save time. The purpose of my reading out the summary yesterday was to provide the context for these follow-up questions and I believe I have tied most of these questions directly to that summary and in certain cases I've had to refer to prior statements. These questions are leading but they are in an effort to move this testimony along expeditiously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Just before the Trial Chamber rules, I in fact had a discussion with my learned friend yesterday, not on this subject but about what exactly was being admitted pursuant to 92 bis. And it's right to say that the statement from which he has just sought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I think if you say 92 bis, you've got it wrong. We are talking of 92 ter at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, but I understand, Your Honour, but the principle is the same. The statement from which he's just sought to lead is not being admitted, as I understand it, pursuant to 92 ter. So it's not so much our objection to him leading from the 92 ter material. It's from material other than the 92 ter material. If I'm wrong about that, no doubt Mr. Thayer will tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not attempting to introduce any other statements other than what we have already admitted into evidence, I understand under Rule 92 ter which is the Rule 61 testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. That's the position. And we really can't follow you -- the logicity of your argument because this being evidence that has already been admitted under Rule 92 ter, it's almost unavoidable.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's my fault. I didn't explain my submission at all properly or well. The whole point is the passage that Mr. Thayer has just put to the witness is not being admitted pursuant to 92 ter. It's a separate statement altogether. That's the basis of our objection. If it formed part of his 92 ter evidence then we couldn't possibly object because clearly that evidence is led by virtue of the 92 ter decision. This is material outside of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is the procedural impediment for Mr. Thayer to make use of this other statement to proceed with the line of questions that arise out of the 92 ter statement that was admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Nothing so far as the 92 ter statement is concerned but material outside of that 92 ter material, the statement that he has just taken the witness to, namely his statement of the 25th and 26th of September of 1995 has not been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And there never will be unless there is a special demand for that and no objection, or -- and justified reason for doing so but it doesn't mean to say that he is not entitled to make use of those statements or the contents of those statements in the -- pursuing a line of questioning with the witness, which arises out of the 61 evidence, Rule 61 evidence that we have admitted under Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We ask rhetorically how does this arise?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think part of the confusion is my learned colleague of the Prosecution on page 9, line 3, he refers to his evidence as 92 bis so our response -- I understand but our response was based on that. Secondly, we believe that we are objecting to the form of the question that he's putting to the witness. It's far too leading in this process to allow him to direct him to the statement so that he could reconfirm his statement and we objected to the form of the question, at least I joined in that basis on the objection. He could ask him what happened on whatever date he wishes, and if the witness doesn't recall then he could possibly redirect him to refresh his recollection, but the Court has previously restricted us when we were either repetitive or outside the scope of questioning. We thought those were the guidelines. That's why we bring it up. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your position would be different in any case because you would be cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think that procedurally, the position is a very simple one. We have already decided that the admission of evidence under Rule 92 bis or Rule 92 ter does not mean that prior to moving to the cross-examination stage, the Prosecution cannot put questions and introduce new areas to the witness. So in so far as the Prosecution is seeking to ask questions on other events that were not covered by the statement -- by the evidence given by the witness under Rule 61 in the Karadzic/Mladic procedure is concerned, I think the Prosecution is very clear. He has got every right to ask whatever questions are relevant. The agreement also has been so far that leading questions will be allowed until and unless one of you stands up and says, "This is a leading question." We may agree or may not agree. And counsel will then proceed according to what we will decide. Now, he definitely has a right to refer the witness to a -- particular statements that he may have made in the past, which were not dealt with or which do not form part of his previous testimony that has been introduced in the records as evidence. In so doing, he must avoid using leading questions now that you have raised the issue of whether it was leading. Yes, in a way, some of the questions the way you put them, were leading questions, so you need now to take into consideration the objection that has been raised and avoid using direct questions in dealing with the witness and in leading the witness. Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Our position is that the minute he refers to the statement, it is immediately a leading question because there is no need to refer the witness to a past statement unless there is a problem with the memory of the witness. If my colleague asks what happened on the 12th of July and the witness says, "I don't remember." "Would you like me to refresh your memory?" "Yes, I would like to." "I will tell you what you said on this occasion in this statement, did you say this, do you recall this? " Then he can move to use a past statement but only if there is a problem with the memory of the witness. If there is no problem with the memory of the witness, then it becomes automatically a leading question, in terms of using and quoting from a statement. Now, we are right now in this Rule 92 ter. This rule is designed to save time. My colleague says he's using this procedure to save time. We are not saving any time. We would be saving any time if my colleague would simply quote the summary of the testimony and open it up for cross-examination. This would be saving time. Right now we are calling it 92 ter, we are opening this so that my colleague has the evidence admitted, and in addition to that, he gets the permission to use that evidence and to get a second confirmation by the witness before opening up for cross-examination. Not only we are not saving time, we are just giving all the rights in the world to the Prosecution and we are not allowing the Defence to do the job that we are supposed to do. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not allowed to do the job you're supposed to do, I don't know, because this definitely doesn't interfere with your rights and you will have all the time that you have indicated you require until we hand down our decision in the near future, distributing in a different manner the time to be used for cross-examination and for examination-in-chief. But in the meantime, the -- you are being very categoric and very radical in your approach. It doesn't mean to say that any reference to a prior statement in the form of a question is necessarily a leading question. I mean, it depends. It depends. When it's a leading question now that you have stood up and objected, we will stop Mr. Thayer, especially if we see you or anyone else standing up again. Otherwise, the rule that we enunciated earlier on, namely that we will proceed unless there is an objection, stands. One other thing is this: That that rule means that anything that is substantial that goes to the heart of the charges, then you shouldn't lead. I mean, you should not use leading questions. I mean, but that I think you are aware of and the understanding is that you try to avoid it. Okay? Yes, Mr. Thayer, I think it's the case of going back to whatever you were referring to from that statement in a somewhat oblique, non-direct manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, understood. I'm clear, Your Honour. I will engage in that five or six question back-and-forth that my learned colleague just described.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Colonel, do you recall your September 1995 statement to the Office of the Prosecutor? Do you recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I can recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall what you said to the investigators at the time concerning the morning of 12 July and any expectations you had about the actions of the VRS that morning?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I stated that I expected that we would be expecting new shelling in the early morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And why did you make that statement to the Office of the Prosecutor at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I indicated at the time that I expected shelling. I had that expectation because the previous day, at the end of the afternoon, at the start of the evening, when dusk was falling, we were shelled near that site. It was -- there were grenade shells and they fell near the refugees, between the houses. It happened twice and my expectation was that in the course of the morning there would be new shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified previously about some conversations that you had with General Mladic on the 12th of July. I'd like to show you now a video clip it's from P02047 at approximately 1 hour 58 minutes. It will last about one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you, sir -- do you see yourself in this video anywhere?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you identify where on the frame you're located?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Absolutely. I'm on the left, and I'm wearing the blue helmet, the blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's the helmet that says "UN"?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And for the record this is at 1 hour 58 minutes, 34.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see General Mladic anywhere in this frame?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe where in the frame he is, sir?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. He's -- appears at the right of the image. He's the second man from the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this is at 1 hour 58 minutes, 40.546 before we move on, there is an individual, sir in a black T-shirt immediately to General Mladic's right. Based on viewing the video clip thus far, can you tell the Trial Chamber who that individual is?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Could you move back a tiny bit on the video so that I can see his face?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We are at 1.58.36.5.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I recognise that man. The man is the interpreter that I had with me at the time. Unfortunately I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may continue, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, we are not receiving a B/C/S interpretation. We can only see English subtitles but our clients are not in a position to follow the video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you receiving interpretation in your language? No. So I think they are perfectly entitled to know what's happening. We need to go back, Mr. Thayer. Be patient all of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, what were you not receiving in your language?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the moment Mr. Thayer made a break and when the video clip was frozen, from that moment on, we lost the sound, the original sound, on the video clip, and the original sound is in B/C/S. This is what we have not been receiving for the past 30 seconds or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But when questions were asked, like could you move back -- like the answer I recognise the man, the man is the interpreter that I had with me at the time, did you get that interpreted in your language?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpretation, as far as the booths are concerned, is functioning perfectly. However, the sound in B/C/S, the original sound that has been recorded, has not reached our clients. We have lost that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back, then, and play it again. You don't need to repeat your questions and answers because those have been interpreted. I think now we ought to play the clip from wherever you started until we have reached --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. It's approximately a minute so it will go quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Did you see it now with sound? Now, General Miletic is indicating that he did not receive the sound? Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MILETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did have the sound but the translation was not good. General Mladic says, "I'm not interested in your commander. We will let go everybody who wants to go." But the translation that I saw was, "We will get everybody go." So this is my remark. The translation services have not translated the words that I've just quoted properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, General. If there are submissions on this that are significant, please go ahead. I invite to you go ahead. Otherwise, let's proceed. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Colonel, did the video clip that you just viewed capture all the conversations you had with General Mladic during that period of time that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I spoke with General Mladic three times, when he arrived at my site.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We won't go into those again, but do you recall what were the exact words that General Mladic used when telling you what he thought of the United Nations at that time?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, in any case he indicated, if I describe it as correctly as I can, that he didn't care one whit about the United Nations, he didn't care a bit about them. At that moment he was the person taking the decisions. These are the words that he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Later that afternoon, sir, did you receive a radio call from Lieutenant Rutten?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I don't know how to phrase this objection but the witness just heard the tape and then we ask him what did he say and he repeats what he just heard on the tape. Where are we going from here, Mr. President? What's the need? Where -- what are we doing? The witness just listened to the tape. He heard what General Mladic said. Then my colleague said, "What did General Mladic say?" Well, I just heard him, I just saw him on this tape say that he didn't care about the united nations? What is the purpose? We are going in circles and we are not going anywhere. This witness has already said that what was in his statements represented the truth. Let's open up for cross-examination, Mr. President and stop wasting time. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But one moment. You say the statement should not even be referred to. The next moment you say what's in the statement is there we don't need to ask him about it. So let's proceed, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll just repeat my prior question, sir. Later that afternoon, did you receive a radio call from Lieutenant Rutten?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed, later that evening I did get a radio call from Lieutenant Rutten and it was a radio call that was about Lieutenant Rutten.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What -- [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Indicated that he was at his position, one of the posts that Bosnian soldiers were arriving there, and that they had started to take away his personal possessions and had started to disarm his group.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you a follow-up call, radio call, later that day concerning Lieutenant Rutten's whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Objection. It's obviously a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why is it leading?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The previous one was as well, the leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where is it leading? I mean, he's just asking whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Because there is no base for this question. Because there is no base for this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is indeed, "Later this afternoon did you receive a radio call from Lieutenant Rutten?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why is it a leading question? Yes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can perhaps help. It's leading he can ask obviously if he received the phone call and what that radio call was but when he asks about the whereabouts -- contents of the conversation were a discussion about his whereabouts so in that sense I think it would be leading and I would join as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then please object in a timely fashion, not two minutes after. There you may be right, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm merely trying to move this examination along. I can ask the foundational, large, open-ended questions and move along but I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Also yesterday you said you had maybe 15 minutes. Today we've been at it for three-quarters of an hour so Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do try not to object as much because I could be on my feet most the day objecting. I thought the Court invited where was the leading and I was just merely pointing it out. But -- since you asked I pointed it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you receive any further radio calls that afternoon concerning any of your men?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you receive any radio calls concerning any of your men who were posted in the area of the bus compound guarding the refugees?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. In this case, this was the situation in relation to the post of Lieutenant Rutten. He had indicated that he had been disarmed, and that his things were being taken away from his people and I was asked to check what the situation of Rutten was at that moment. That was the nature of the radio call.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What if anything did you do in response to that call, sir?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I went to the location of Rutten and his group. I worked there. And I saw from a distance that the group of Lieutenant Rutten was being guarded and they had no longer had their things. They no longer had their weapons. Lieutenant Rutten gave me a sign from the distance that I had to stay at a distance so as not also to run the risk of having my things taken away from me, possibly to be held there at the place by those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just to -- just for the record, to eliminate any possibility of a confusion, page 19, line 14, relating to the first telephone conversation or radio conversation with Lieutenant Rutten, we have there indicated that he was at his position, one of the post that Bosnian soldiers were arriving there. I think let's clarify it whether these were Bosnian Muslim soldiers or whether these were Bosnian Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you understand Mr. President's question, Lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, for clarity, they were Bosnian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Again, sir, when you say Bosnian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are now receiving interpretation in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you referring to Bosnian Serb soldiers or Bosnian Muslim soldiers arriving at Lieutenant Rutten's position?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I'm talking of Bosnian Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to turn your attention to my last couple of questions. During the evening of 12 July, you testified previously that VRS soldiers started to take the belongings of the DutchBat soldiers who were guarding the refugees in the area of the bus station. Would you tell the Trial Chamber whether that happened to you as well or not?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of the night, we were outside with the refugees, and at a certain moment in the night I was pulled up by the Bosnian Serb -- by soldier accompanied by another Bosnian Serb soldier, who wanted to have my things. They wanted to have my equipment and everything belonging to it, my flak jacket, my helmet, et cetera. And of course I didn't agree with this. So there was a quite a fierce discussion and we were shouting at each other. I did not want to surrender my things. He absolutely wanted to have my things. He was making that very clear, and I tried to indicate in is various languages, Dutch, English, that I did not want to surrender my things. Subsequently, the Bosnian Serb soldier pushed the barrel of his Kalashnikov in my stomach and threatened me to surrender my things forthwith. I got even more angry. I pointed out to him that he would not get my things and that I would report this to the local commander at that moment, the Bosnian Serb commander of the moment, and I mentioned, shouted the names of Miki and Mane and I saw him hesitate at that moment and his colleague also indicated to him that they had to leave me alone and subsequently they left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did he have a distinguishable rank? The soldier? Was he an ordinary soldier or did he have any insignia that would denote his rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see any insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you just mentioned the names Mane and Miki. Did you in fact meet these two individuals?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I met those two persons. This was in the evening, the evening before, when Lieutenant van Duijn who at that moment was a temporary commander of the location and I was there to bring a report to the compound. When I returned, Lieutenant van Duijn introduced me to these two people indicating that they, there, at that moment, were in charge, and Miki and Mane, that was the way I met them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe Mane, please?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. If I describe him, then I'm speaking of a man who is somewhat shorter than myself, black hair, he was quite firmly built, solidly built, solid face.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was Mane's role, as you saw it, at that time?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: They were the local Bosnian Serb commanders and in that respect, Mane had more of a leading role over Miki.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Finally, sir, I'd like to show you again Exhibit P02047. It's a video clip. And it begins at 2 hours, 26 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the individual in the middle of the frame at 2 hours 26 minutes 11.8 wearing the blue vest?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise him as the person who was designated with the name Miki.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the individual that is now depicted at the far left of the screen, the male?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. That is the person Mane.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This is at 2 hours 26 minutes 29.4 seconds. Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Thayer. Now, have you come to an agreement who is going first? Mr. Zivanovic, as usual?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will be the first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic is lead counsel defending Colonel Popovic in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Mr. Koster, when you returned from Srebrenica in 1995, you filled out a questionnaire that was provided to you by The Hague Tribunal. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I can recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have the questionnaire in question and I would kindly ask for the Exhibit 1D50 to be presented to the witness. Very well. Now, you have it on the screen in front of you. Do you recognise the handwriting? In other words, is this your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise the handwriting. That is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The copy of the statement that I have and that is in English does not contain your signature. I kindly ask you now to tell me whether you yourself signed this questionnaire once you filled it out.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: And now you are referring to the English questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The English questionnaire, because this is the only copy that I have. Did you fill out the questionnaire in Dutch, in English or in both languages?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. If you refer to the English questionnaire, I can't remember whether I did or did not sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you sign the Dutch version of the questionnaire? Did you have a questionnaire in Dutch?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: There were several questionnaires but I don't recall whether there was a Dutch questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, do you remember the time when you filled out the questionnaire, at least approximately, because the questionnaire does not bear any date.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I can't say that for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you answer truthfully when you filled out the questionnaire, and were your answers based on your best recollection at the time?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Naturally, I filled in the questionnaires in accordance with the truth and to my best capacity at that moment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please look at page 4 of the questionnaire that you filled out? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the first part, there is a question: Did you personally see inhuman or cruel treatment? Can you see that? It says, "did you personally witness inhuman or cruel treatment?" Your answer was no. You crossed out the possible answer yes, which means that your answer is no.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then the question was did you personally witness a summary execution? Your answer was yes, but you also noted that you only saw the victims of the execution, but not the act of execution itself. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you stated that you personally didn't witness a rape; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct. I did not witness rapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you personally did not witness an act of torture?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I did not see tortures at the time, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But it says that you did see wanton destruction or theft of private property; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And finally, you stated that you personally did not witness any other gross violations of human rights?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's how it reads, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And finally, after that, you provided a description of the bodies that you saw, and you responded to those questions by the Prosecutor in detail.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I see that written.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me whether you stand by what you have written here? Can you please confirm if this is correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: If the question is whether it's accurate if we look at gross violations of human rights, I just mentioned that we experienced shelling, we were under fire, so I don't know why I indicated no there because that would appear to be a violation of human rights, shelling -- firing grenades near refugees would appear to be a violation of human rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And are you claiming that the refugees were a direct target of shelling?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's how it seemed to me. The shells fell 50 to 75 metres away from us in the immediate vicinity of the refugees. That's why I stated earlier that we expected that we would come under fire in the course of the following morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But there were no wounded then from the shells?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: There were an awful lot of injured at the time that we were trying to help but I can't immediately determine whether they were injured as a result of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also recall giving a statement to the Dutch authorities on the 11th of September 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you gave a statement to The Hague Tribunal investigators on the 25th and the 26th of September of 1995.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to remind you of some things that you said in those statements or to be more specific in the statement to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal on the 25th and the 26th of September 1995, and I'm just going to ask you if you recall saying that and if it's correct that you said that or not. I'm going to show you the parts, relevant parts, of the statement so that you can see your own words. Do you recall stating that in June 1995, you met twice with the mayor of Srebrenica, and negotiated on food shortages and some other matters?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I remember the meeting and as far as I can remember, I described the man as the mayor of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that you negotiated about food?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. We negotiated about food.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall saying that from mid-June 1995, on visiting Srebrenica, you noticed each time more and more armed Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall stating that they were -- or some of them were dressed in camouflage uniforms while others only had parts of uniforms? They were wearing some civilian clothing and some uniforms, for example, the army coats or army shirts?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you also recall stating that you saw certain armed people in civilian clothes, who wore civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you also recall stating that on the 10th of July, in the evening, you were on an assignment at a cross roads near Potocari when you saw four Muslim fighters in camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall them telling you that that evening, the Muslim population would not come to Potocari and if they tried to do so, they would prevent them?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall stating that after that, in that same place, a Muslim commander came, he was the commander of the northern part of the enclave, Mandic?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember meeting him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You talked with him for about 45 minutes?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that after he left, you said that a Muslim fighter came and called you to come to a small headquarters of theirs that was located in the basement of a house?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you went there?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I went there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that you also said that you saw the first groups of refugees in Potocari on the 11th of July at about 3.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall saying that amongst them you saw one or two persons who were armed?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more question and then we could go on a break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Do you recall stating that amongst the refugees in the compound, your compound, there were psychiatric patients from the local hospital who were moving around and that they were making the atmosphere among the refugees worse?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I suggest that this is a good point to go on our break, and then I can continue afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We will have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Koster, you have just confirmed -- I just counted -- about eight things that were in your statement to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal on the 25th and the 26th of September 1995. Of course, you recall that on the 4th of July 1996, you appeared before this Tribunal for the first time as a witness. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct if I were to tell you that by comparing your statement and your testimony before the Tribunal, you did not mention any of these matters or questions when you testified as a witness before the Tribunal. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Would the interpreter please repeat the question one more time? Because the question was very confusing. I only want to listen to the interpretation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll repeat it. All of these things -- would you like me to repeat my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, having heard you, the witness, the interpreters, it is definitely the case of repeating the question, perhaps in a little bit more clear manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's like this: All of these things from your statement that I mentioned to you before the break and which you confirmed as having said, none of these things I found in the transcript of your testimony in the Karadzic and Mladic case on the 4th of July 1996. So I'm asking you if this is correct that none of these matters were discussed by you then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you trying to justify the length of the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not quite, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please answer the question. It's being put to you that what you had in your statements, which preceded the -- your testimony in the 61 -- Rule 61 proceedings was not repeated during that testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that. I would need to see the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to be more precise if it's the case, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you the relevant parts. Do you recall that in the Karadzic/Mladic case, proceedings on the 4th of July 1996, you did not say that there were psychiatric patients among the refugees who had been released from the local institution, that they were walking around amongst the refugees and making the situation worse?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't remember that I didn't say that, and I would need to see the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's very hard for me to show you. I mean, I can show you the whole testimony, the whole transcript of your testimony. That's Exhibit 46 of the Defence. However, it's a long document and it's in English. The only solution would be for you to read the whole transcript and to say if you talked about this or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's try and solve it in another manner. Mr. Thayer do you contest what is being put to the witness by Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I think we can all agree that those matters were not raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Colonel, I think you can now answer the question taking into consideration the statement made by the Prosecutor that indeed, reading through your testimony in the Rule 61 proceedings, you never made reference to this. Well, the Karadzic/Mladic proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to go through the other topics, not just the matter of the patients. Does the witness also recall that on that occasion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's a sequence of questions, trying to elicit from the witness an answer, "Yes, I agree with you, these eight issues or matters that I had referred to in my statements, I did not repeat during my testimony," I think we can shorten that and then proceed straight with the question that you need to ask him, because I mean, there is a simple answer to that. Mr. Thayer wouldn't have spent an hour asking him about those issues if they had been included in the Rule 61 testimony in any case. We wouldn't have allowed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question: Does the witness recall that he also did not mention this in the Krstic case either, where he appeared as a witness?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't remember not stating that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If it saves time I can state that it was not raised in the Krstic rebuttal testimony of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to ask the witness now is the following:

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell me whether then, in those cases, or more specifically in your testimony to date before this Tribunal, you did not discuss these matters or did somebody ask you to do it like that, to act like that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We didn't get interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness was not audible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Colonel, you need to repeat your answer, please, because the interpreters did not hear you. Could you be kind enough to repeat? The question was, I'll repeat it in case you did not receive it. Are you able to tell me whether then in those cases or more specifically in your testimony to date before this Tribunal, you did not discuss these matters or did somebody ask you to do it like that, to act like that? Basically what is being elicited from you is do you have an explanation why, when you testified, both in Krstic and in the Karadzic/Mladic, Rule 61 proceedings, you did not make reference to these eight points? Do you have an explanation? Could it possibly be because someone told you not to mention them? This is what you're being asked, if I have reproduced your question faithfully. If not, Mr. Zivanovic, please correct me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I understand the question better. There were several answers in there. I was not asked not to mention various things. The reason why they were not mentioned by me is because there were either insufficient questions about them or because I couldn't remember them at the time. Either one is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be all, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Zivanovic. Who is going next? Mr. Ostojic, who is standing next to you, will be cross-examining you now. He represents Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Beara we have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Ostojic. Who is next? Madam Nikolic is representing, what's your rank again, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel as well. She is representing Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Second Lieutenant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Second Lieutenant. I promoted you. Yes, Madam Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, we have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic is representing Mr. Borovcanin. I am renouncing to ranks now. It's become difficult and complicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, actually we do have quite some questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Koster. On the 11th of September 1995, you had a debriefing at the Dutch royal army. We have this debriefing. It has been tendered into the evidence. It's entered into e-court. And I wanted to put a number of questions to you relating to your answers to the questions that were put to you in the debriefing. While responding to questions on the equipment of Muslim fighters in the enclave, you said that they used radio communications when communicating with one another. Can you please confirm that before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This assertion of yours is based on your personal knowledge that you personally had the opportunity to see Muslim fighters communicating with each other by radio. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In your statement, i.e., in the debriefing provided to the Dutch government, on page 9, you say this and I'm going to read it to you. "The use of items of kit belonging to Dutch UN military personnel by Serbs in particular never gave the impression that they were trying to pass themselves off as Dutch UN military personnel. He was not aware of any misuse of, example UN insignia, the Red Cross, et cetera, et cetera. He had not noticed that any mines had been laid." [Interpretation] Could you please confirm before this Trial Chamber that the statement you provided in the debriefing to the Dutch government is correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you speak about laying mines, this statement of yours obviously refers to the army of Republika Srpska, wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any information about the Muslim side laying mines, either in the enclave or outside of it?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't have any such data.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Earlier today, my colleague, Zivanovic, informed you about the content of the statement that you provided to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal on the 25th and the 26th of September. I would like to go over some ground again. He already asked you about the accuracy of your statement and your recollection of the events, and he asked you about the increased number of Muslim fighters during the month of June 1995, which is something that you yourself could observe. With this regard, I would like to confront you with one part of your statement. This is on page 6, paragraph 3, and it reads, "[In English] At that time we were no longer able to fulfil the policy requirements of demilitarised zone. By this I mean that there were so many Muslim fighters walking about armed that UN soldiers were incapable of disarming these people." [Interpretation] Could you again confirm that the conclusion that you provided in the statement is correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 7 of the same statement, paragraphs 3 and 4, you stated this. Since the date is not precise, I would like to say that the date in question is either the 8th or 9th July 1995. This is what you state: "[In English] After driving 100 or 200 metres, this vehicle was stopped by about ten Muslim fighters. The spokesman of the Muslim fighters spoke to Sergeant van Renssen. The Muslim fighter said that the armoured vehicle could not go any further and that they should return to observation post F. Sergeant van Renssen decided nevertheless to carry on to Srebrenica. The Muslim spokesman then told him that they would be fired at it -- at then. They did so. At the moment when my fellow soldiers drew away, one much the Muslim fighters threw a hand grenade at the vehicle. Private Renssen was then seated in the vehicle's gunner position. A grenade fragment hit the back of his head and he later died at the compound as a result of these injuries." [Interpretation] Mr. Koster, is this a correct and accurate interpretation of the events that led to the death of Private Renssen?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Those are the events as I know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This is a fair answer. In other words, you know that Muslim fighters prevented members of the DutchBat from withdrawing from observation points and that they even fired at them, which resulted in the deaths of some of them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be an interpretation issue but there is an a reference to deaths and I believe the testimony so far in this case has referred to one death, that of Private van Renssen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I don't have a problem with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you followed the discussion? We are referring to only one death, not several.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The death of Private Renssen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's clear enough. Thank you. Do you think you need to repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe not necessary. I'll move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you provided to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal, you spoke about witnessing a suicide that happened on the UN base between the 12th and the 13th, and that you personally, together with some other colleagues from the DutchBat, cut the rope around the unfortunate man's neck. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: You ask whether I remember this at the UN base but it wasn't at the UN base. I'm not sure whether it's a problem of understanding but it was off the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us say that this was outside the UN base, but in any case, you witnessed the event. You were the one together with others who actually took that man from the rope that he was hanging from?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I didn't see the act of suicide in progress. I found the man and then we did indeed cut the man loose.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Stay assured that I'm not interested in any other details. I'm just interested in whether you were aware of the fact that somebody did commit suicide. From some other witnesses, we heard there were other death cases during the days of the 12th, the 13th and during the night between the -- those two days, before the refugees were evacuated, that a woman died in child birth, and so on and so forth. Are you aware of any other death cases among the refugees in and around that area where the refugees were accommodated at the time?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I do know about deaths on the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My next question arises from this: What happened with the bodies of those people who died either on the base or around the base?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: If my memory serves me, I believe that they were buried there temporarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you say "there," could you please be more precise? Where is "there"? Is it on the base, around the base, close to a stream? Could you please be more precise and explain what you mean when you say "there"?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'll go into details. As far as I'm concerned, it's on the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You personally did not take part in those burials, did you?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But some other members of the DutchBat were involved in the burials or maybe not, maybe the refugees buried the bodies themselves?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know whether a report was drafted by UN troops with regard to the number of people who died, their identity, the reasons for their death, in other words, did you, as members of DutchBat, not you personally but somebody else, kept any kind of record on those incidents?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'll tell you what I know. I know that the compound management indicated that the man who hanged himself had to be returned to the compound because that was where the record was kept as to how many people died.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who was in charge of keeping records on the number of people who died?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know which persons did that, but I know that the compound management issued instructions to keep such a register.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. When you use the term, "Compound management," are you referring to the DutchBat? Would that be a fair translation of the term "compound management"?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On several occasions you've mentioned the name of Major Momir Nikolic. How many times did you see Major Nikolic on the 12th and 13th of July in Potocari? I'm repeating major's name again because we have another gentleman by the same name of Nikolic so how many times did you see Major Momir Nikolic in Potocari on those two days?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I saw Major Nikolic when the Bosnian Serb military arrived at my site near the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You have already testified to that effect. However, did you see him on any other occasion during those two days, on the 12th and the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the event when Major Nikolic was in Potocari on the 12th. If I understand your testimony, he was among the first members of the Serb forces who approached the refugees in Potocari. Did I understand your testimony well?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: You understood that correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Escorted by the UN troops, he made a round of the group of refugees in order to see how many men there were, how many women, what their state was and so on and so forth; is that the true representation of the situation?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what was your impression of the position that Momir Nikolic held within the Serbian army structure once they arrived in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know what his position was at the moment the military came in. I know what his position was the moment they weren't in. He was the local commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This is a fair answer, I'd say. I would like to move on to another topic, and this is the place where you claim having seen the bodies of nine persons who had been killed. First of all, I would like to read back to you what you said in your statement to the OTP on the 25th and 26th September, on page 12 -- I apologise, page 15, paragraph 1 of the English version of your statement. "At one stage I briefly returned to the compound where I heard a rumour about bodies lying about somewhere. When I was back at the refugees location, Rutten and van Schaik came up to me and told me that they'd been told the rough location of the bodies. I walked with them to the west of the road where the refugees were being loaded into buses." [Interpretation] Do you remember this part of your statement? This is a quote from your statement. You said that you were moving westward to the place where the refugees were loaded into buses. How far was it when you turned westward from the place where the refugees were being loaded into buses?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I would have to estimate that. I believe it was around 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I assume that when we are talking about the place where refugees were being loaded into buses, that you're talking about the place where there were four APCs that provided some sort of a channeling for the refugees. Is that the place that you are referring to when you say that the refugees were being loaded into buses?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That was that location, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When, together with Lieutenant Rutten and van Schaik set off, did you have to go through the barricade composed of the four APCs?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: In as far as I recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when you passed the barricade, behind the barricade there were Muslim refugees. Is this correct? In other words, you had to go through the crowd of Muslim refugees in order to go that way; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to show you the aerial image of Potocari. This is Exhibit P01516. [In English] Could we get it from e-court, please. Thanks. That's the document. [Interpretation] Mr. Koster, I assume that you're familiar with this photo, the same photo was used in your preparation for this testimony, when you were prepared by the OTP. Please use the pen that is next to you. This is the marker pen that can be used to mark the image, can you please mark the point where the refugees were being loaded into buses and where the four APCs were that formed the barricade?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: This would have been approximately in this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And in order for us to have a clearer picture of what has been marked, can you write down "four APCs" next to the marking?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can you draw a line showing the route that you took as you were moving to the place where you claim you found the bodies of the nine dead people?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: You want me to draw this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please sign this photo and put today's date on it?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just let me make sure of one thing with this witness. To the north of where you marked the document, there is a road. That leads to where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this the road you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
