utterances.text: The road on top of where you marked with a square. What direction would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the road to Srebrenica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but which is the way to Srebrenica, which is the way to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up is to Srebrenica, and towards the bottom is to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, could you draw another thing on the map? Where was this car dealership or car service [as interpreted] that has been mentioned on a number of occasions in this case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer? I was waiting to see the witness mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just for clarification purposes, Your Honour, I don't believe that there has been testimony about a car dealership in the case. I may be mistake be. I'm just not sure that that's actually in the record. If there is a reference --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a translation matter then. I was not referring to any car dealer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could be -- could you be specific now to which part of the transcript you're referring to, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it has to do with some previous testimonies and with the location of the refugees where they have been held and some of the witnesses mentioned a bus service or bus station or something of the kind. That's what I was referring to that, it was obviously some mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Bus compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Bus compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, that's how -- if my recollection is correct, that's how it has been described or referred to before, bus compound. Do you recall the existence of a bus compound in the vicinity there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And do you wish him to mark it on the photo?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would love to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we don't need this map any more. Thank you. And I won't have any more questions about this particular issue for this witness. However, Mr. Koster, in your statement to the Prosecution on 25 and 26 September 1995, on page 15, paragraph 1, when you speak about the bodies that you allegedly found in the meadow, you say this: "[In English] In a meadow by a small river I saw nine bodies, sorry, nine persons lying on their bellies with their heads bent forward." [Interpretation] This is a quote from your statement given to the Prosecutor's Office on the 25th and 26th. What you said to the Prosecution at the time, does it still stand? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I would either like the statement written -- read out to me again or I would like to take another look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course. There is a possibility to quickly check this in e-court. This is on page 15, paragraph 1, and, just one second, I wanted to find the number, and I think that it's 1D44. [In English] It's on page 15, paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: And you asked me whether I stick by that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And if it's correct, what you were stating at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Later, I recalled that two persons were on their sides in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So at the time when you talked about this, you didn't mention that two persons were lying on their side, but that all nine of them were lying on their belly. Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, that is what I recalled. At the time, that is what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I understand that later you recollected better than when you provided that statement in 1995.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Later, yes, indeed, I remembered that two persons were on their sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I would like to talk a little bit about those nine persons that you say you found on the meadow. Amongst the nine bodies that you say you found, was any of those bodies known to you? Did you know any of those people?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I did know these persons -- not know these persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you see their face? Because you said that they were lying down on their bellies with their heads tucked forwards. Did you ever see their faces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did indeed see the faces but did not recognise any people, if that's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. However, this opens up another question. In the same statement to the Prosecutor of the 25th and the 26th of September 1995, also on page 15, paragraph 1, you said you did not turn the bodies over when they were lying on their bellies so obviously it was impossible for you to see their faces. Shall we look at your statement of the 25th and the 26th of September 1995, paragraph 1 on page 15 again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you still have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have the text in front of me but you're asserting that I could not have seen their faces or was this a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. The question is you will recall that just a minute ago I asked you whether you saw their faces and you answered yes. And when I asked you that question, I had in mind what you had stated earlier on, as appears from this statement, namely, "I did not turn any of them over." So if they were lying down on their bellies with their head tucked forward, and you never turned them over, how could you see their faces? This is basically what is being -- what you're being confronted with by Mr. Lazarevic. And you can confirm that you said, "I did not turn any of them." It's exactly halfway through the first full paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Actually, if the faces are concerned if people are lying on their front their faces are somewhat to the side usually so that is why I did get a look at the faces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you explain it? I didn't quite understand your answer. As far as the faces are concerned, this is how the transcript goes, "if the faces are concerned, if people are lying on their front, their faces are somewhat to the side, usually, so that is why I did get a look at the faces." Basically you're meaning that you looked at part of the faces but not the full face? All right. That is okay. You saw what you could see in the circumstances, part of the face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that you saw their faces, it didn't mean anything to you because you didn't know these people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I didn't recognise the men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Move to the next question, Mr. Lazarevic, because I think it's a useless question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And of course you don't know whether those people were Serbs or Muslims, you could not know that, since you didn't know those people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And on the basis of your testimony here, you don't know when those people were killed?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time but I know that they hadn't been dead for very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's fair. But you don't know, since you didn't see that personally, in which circumstances those people were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And of course, you don't know who killed those people. You cannot know that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I didn't see it happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Today, you spoke how -- about how some documents were found next to those bodies. I think I looked very carefully at all the documents relating to this incident that you described, and I understood that these documents were taken by your colleague, van Schaik, warrant officer van Schaik and not yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And warrant officer van Schaik at no point in time compared the documents, the identity in those documents, with the actual persons that were found on this meadow? He didn't check the documents with the actual persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I didn't see him do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment because.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not hear any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We did not get any interpretation. I was waiting but it never arrived. You need to repeat your question again because we did not understand it in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And besides not -- besides the fact that warrant officer van Schaik did not compare the ID documents with the persons whom you found there, and this wasn't done by yourself or by your colleague Rutten either, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I just said that he didn't -- I didn't see him do that. He could have done it but I didn't see him doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we know that they were ID documents? Because I don't think that was specifically stated by the witness. He just said documents without specifying what kind of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still didn't get my -- the answer to my previous question whether you yourself actually checked the documents against the bodies and was this done by your colleague Rutten?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I didn't do it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, as for the documents that were found there, how many documents were found all together?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figure. As a rough estimate I would say that Major van Schaik took -- he took three or four or five pieces of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I checked what van Schaik also testified on this matter, so it more or less tallies, but can you please tell us what the documents looked like, these documents in that number that you found there?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The documents looked like text documents, and their layout appeared to be official.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The text in the documents was in B/C/S, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I couldn't read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. There is no need to speculate on this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one basic question: Did these documents contain any photos? Were there any photos on them or images of persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no photographs on the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you told us in your testimony that you knelt there and that Lieutenant Rutten took a few photographs, but when this film was developed back in Holland, it was destroyed so the photographs taken by van Rutten of you next to the bodies do not exist. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'm aware that the photographs were lost during the development process.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I were to summarise the answers you gave to previous questions, please, now I'm going to do that and tell me if something of that is not true. You told us that you found nine bodies on a meadow, you don't know if they were Serb or Muslims, you don't know when, in which circumstances and by whom these people were killed, that you found documents, that you don't know if they belonged to those persons or not, and that photographs were taken in that place that do not exist. Is there anything incorrect in my summary of your answers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that the photographs don't exist. I just know that they were lost during the development process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I don't want to stand on formality, Your Honour, that is a long question. If he could just -- be offered the opportunity to really read it and if it is a compound problem for him, I just ask that he be allowed to take his time to answer that. That was a lot of items in one question, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so, yeah. I mean, go ahead, your next question, I think we can live with that. In fact I am surprised Mr. Bourgon did not stand up to object. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After you were in this meadow, as you said, and you described the circumstances saying that you were seen by a Serbian soldier who had a radio with him, that there was some shooting and that you took the same road back, and fearing for your safety, you saw, and judging by what you say in your debriefing of the 11th of September 1995, you saw somebody being carried on a stretcher by somebody. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you say -- I assume that you don't know the person that was on the stretcher. Was it a soldier or a civilian? Can you at least determine that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I don't remember the person on the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the persons carrying the stretcher? I assume it was two people, these two people who were carrying the stretcher, were they soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I can remember the stretcher was on wheels, and there were DutchBat soldiers present there and we joined them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the persons who were carrying the stretcher or, if it was a wheeled stretcher, they were pushing it, are you saying that these were soldiers from DutchBat? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I stated that there were DutchBat soldiers present and that we joined them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just so that the transcript is clear, were those soldiers carrying the stretcher? Members of DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you also pick up a stretcher and pretend to be helping and in that way reach the UN compound, fearing for your safety? Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: We joined the stretcher because we did not want to stand out and I didn't reach the UN compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did those people with the stretcher get to the UN base? Did you separate off earlier? Did you follow them for as long as they were carrying this stretcher with this person? Can you recall anything of that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I remember remaining at the site of the APCs and that Major van Schaik and Lieutenant Rutten went along.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just this second part of the question, did you perhaps see where the stretcher went?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The stretcher headed in the direction of the compound but I didn't see where it ended up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any further questions on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Not regarding this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because we need to have an early break so we'll have the break now and it will be a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Isn't the person you've mentioned, just mentioned, enjoying protective measures? So let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you can start all over again without repeat. We are in open session, Mr. Thayer. I understand you have a scheduling problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Mr. President. Colonel Koster will be unavailable for tomorrow's session. We intend to pick up with the next scheduled witness tomorrow. We suggest that after we've had an opportunity to communicate through the victim witness unit, with Colonel Koster, that we will schedule his return as soon as possible for resumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me take it up from here. Mr. Lazarevic, how much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Not more than ten minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between 30 and 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic or Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Less than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we went make it but I'm always optimistic. Mr. Lazarevic, cut it down to five, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Minutes, not hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Koster, perhaps we can go through the rest of your testimony with me quickly so that we don't take up so much time. I would like to move to a topic that's different in relation to the topics that we've covered so far. It's about the separation of men from the crowd of refugees. In your statement to the Prosecution, of the 25th and the 26th of September 1995, on page 12, last paragraph, you stated that you had heard from Rutten about the separation but that you also personally saw Serbian soldiers breaking through the DutchBat cordon and going in the direction of the buses. You stated that on page 12, last paragraph of your statement. Is that a correct description what you saw, that the Serbs were going through the cordon put up by the United Nations, separating off a group of men, and then returning?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'd like to see the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Inaudible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to see the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have the statement of yours in the system on page 12, it's 1D44 or 45, I'm not quite sure for this one. 44. Last paragraph and here it says, "I saw the Serbian soldiers pushing these people toward the buses but before that I saw Serbian soldier breaking through our cordon and taking a group of about 100 Muslim people in the direction of the buses." [Interpretation] Do you confirm the correctness of your assertion?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that is what you saw; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the same statement, on page 14, last paragraph, talking about the situation amongst the Muslim refugees at that point in time, you said the following: [In English] "At that moment, everyone in the Muslim population was looking out for him or herself." [Interpretation] Do you see that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you adhere by that statement?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you well when you say that the refugees, the huge mass of refugees that tried looking after themselves as best as they could, had the main objective to get to the buses as quickly as possible and to be taken to the territory under the control of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know to which area they were supposed to depart at that point. I know that some of the population was pushing and another part of the population was more -- was standing aside and was waiting to see, was more reluctant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Did you at one point in time, on the 12th of July, before the human shield was established, attend a stampede of the refugees who had spotted the buses and started running towards them? And was it easy to control the situation at the time or was it difficult?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the last part of the question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In practical terms, this is a two-part question. Did you see this stampede of the refugees as they were rushing towards the buses?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since some other members of the DutchBat testified to that effect I decided to ask you that. My next question is this: Was it difficult to control that huge crowd of refugees who wanted to get to the buses as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. It was difficult. People were pushing and jostling and when they headed towards the buses they were rushed by the Bosnian Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You were shown the photos of a person whom you identified as Mane and another one whom you identified as Miki, and you denoted them as Serb commanders. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, I don't know if this is an interpretation or a mistake or not. I don't recall the Colonel ever saying that they were both commanders. I think as far as Mane is concerned, yes, he did say so, but I'm not that sure that he ever described Miki as a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I may be wrong but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My case manager will check in a moment in the transcript but any way in his statement given to the OTP on 25th of September, on page 13, he says, he says, he introduced me to two of the Serb's duty commanders named Miki and Mane. So I basically have the knowledge of him referring to them as commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I was referring to I mean those statements I've never read and I don't think any of us have read them because we don't read them but I was referring to the transcript of the testimony too that we've heard here. But any way, please proceed assuming that you accept that both Mane and Miki were commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or duty commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was just advised by Mr. Meek that it's on page 23, line 14 of today's transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I have to repeat the question, let me put it this way: You talked about Miki and Mane as duty commanders, local commanders, in Potocari. Do you remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Miki was a foot soldier who was an interpreter, he served as an interpreter there, would that change your understanding of the whole situation involving the two men?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Not to me. At the time, he appeared to me as one of the people in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. I would like to go back to that footage of Miki and Mane that we have already seen on e-court. This is page 02047. The time between 0224 to 022501.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we stop now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you have already recognised Miki and Mane and I believe that you will agree with me that the gentleman on the left is Mr. van Duijn. Here, captain Mane addresses Miki asking him to translate his words and says, "To check and see whether anybody wants to go. It is their job." When he says it's their job, he refers to the DutchBat. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I don't believe that there has been a foundation laid that Colonel Koster was present for this particular conversation. I showed him the clip for the purpose of identifying the individuals but I don't know if he -- if we have a foundation laid to interpret what was going on in the conversation, and what was meant by the various parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose he can -- let's hear the next question because that is actually what will put us in a position to give weight or not to your objection. Doesn't mean to say that if he wasn't there he cannot answer questions based on what he can see here. So let's hear the question and then we'll see whether to take up your objection again and decide it. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I could have asked this question in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, was one of the tasks of the DutchBat to establish among the refugees who wanted to leave Potocari and go to Kladanj and who on the other hand didn't want to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As far as you know, obviously.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we proceed with this video just for one second?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And obviously, in reference to your answer, was a task of the DutchBat to collect those Muslims in Potocari who wanted to leave and to put them on the buses?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. That's not known to me. All I know is that it was our duty to protect the refugees and to avert as much suffering as we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the aversion of their suffering, wouldn't that also mean helping those who wanted to leave Srebrenica to get on the buses and enabling them to leave Srebrenica if they so wanted?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I stand by my previous statement, our only task there as far as I know was to avert suffering as best we could while the refugees were being transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. I would now like to go to another video clip that has been shown to you, depicting General Mladic. You spoke about that meeting and you recognised yourself in the video. When this video clip was shown to you, you said that General Mladic said that he couldn't care less about the United Nations. Can we go back to that video clip and see what General Mladic said exactly? [In English] 15725 to 15750. Can we go just back for a moment? A bit more?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Here, General Mladic says "I couldn't care less about your commander." He spoke about your commander, not about the United Nations in general terms. He wasn't referring to the United Nations as an institution, wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Apparently he's saying that in this part of the conversation that was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that he has repeated that sentence on several occasions? He didn't just say it once?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I had several conversations with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we continue showing the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a bit. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here you can see the same situation. This was all recorded in one go, the whole clip, and here Mladic says, "Whoever wishes to be transported will be transported." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I see that it says that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it then clear that Mladic says, clear and loud, that all those who wish to leave will be transported? He never says, "You must leave." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I see what the text reads, but I cannot infer whether he said it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. However, when it comes to your role in the entire situation, I would like to show you just one part of your statement, i.e., the debriefing, 1D00045, on page 1 of that debriefing, towards its very end you say, it is said about you, "[In English] The witness received orders to cooperate with the evacuation and to try to supervise it as well as possible so as to prevent any excess." [Interpretation] A reference is made to the orders that you received with regard to the evacuation. Could you please confirm that what you said in your debriefing is correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: What part of the debriefing is that from?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The last -- actually, the penultimate sentence, the very end of that page, "[In English] The witness received orders to cooperate with the evacuation and to try to supervise it as well as possible so as to prevent any excess."

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, you adhere by what you said?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And only a couple more questions about the events that ensued once all the refugees left the base. Could you please tell us briefly how -- can you please describe in brief terms the appearance of the base and the area around the base once the refugees left in late afternoon hours on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. If I remember correctly, there was luggage everywhere, equipment of people, along the road, sometimes on the road, and it was also lying about the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was it who finally removed those things, destroyed them or did whatever with them?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Which items?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The ones that you've just mentioned, the personal effects, the luggage, the bags of food, the blankets, whatever was left behind.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You don't know. Very well. I would like to go back to something that you already mentioned on your cross. You said that you were there when you were outside the base to attend to the person who had killed himself. Can you tell us exactly where this was? Was it in one of the factories, in a house? Where was the body hanging?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, the body was hanging in a small building in the vicinity of the factory, and the factory is not the compound, and the building had no roof but there were concrete or in any case there were beams there possibly concrete on the top of the building and on those was the rope with which the man had hung himself and the building was full of excrement, people's excrement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions and I would like to thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Madam Fauveau, who is representing General Miletic, will now cross-examine you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Colonel Koster, you talked about the Muslim fighters who were in the enclave. Is it fair to say that they shot at the Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I never saw this myself. However, I received reports that this is in fact what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in that way, the Muslims -- the Muslim fighters provoked the Serbs and the Serbs started shooting?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: In the reports which I received there, with some regularity, counterfire was received from the Bosnian Serb side, yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you agree with me that what the Muslim fighters were doing was a form of provocation?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know which purpose that sort of fire had.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that when you arrived in Potocari in January 1995, you had been briefed by Major Franken, the situation in the DutchBat, and how DutchBat was being resupplied?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that on that occasion, in January 1995, Major Franken told you that there was a fuel problem already then?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I understood at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You stated today that you received fuel in June of 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that the HCR fuel was in the DutchBat base located in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that DutchBat at some point in time used this fuel which was stocked by the UNHCR?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'm aware of that. This was agreed with the people of UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In April 1995, were you on leave?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I was on leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you returned to Potocari on the 21st of April 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date but I know that indeed it was April when I returned to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But that was rather during the second half of April, wasn't it, if you can -- if you remember?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we show the witness Exhibit number 1D44, please? This is a statement dated September 1995 and given to the OTP. Can we turn to page 4, please? I'd like you to look at the first sentence in paragraph 2. "[In English] From 7 to 21 April 1995 I had two weeks' leave." [Interpretation] This statement was given in September 1995. Do you allow for the fact that at that time you must have remembered exactly at what date you returned to the enclave?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did DutchBat receive reports coming from the other front lines in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That is very well possible. I myself did not have them in my hands. I did not see them but quite regularly we had briefings about the situation around us.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you knew that there was fighting around Sarajevo in June?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember that at some point in time there was fighting in Krajina, in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I know there were such fights in the Krajina. However, I don't recall exactly when this was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember that the supply convoys could not get through, couldn't reach Srebrenica because of that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I no longer recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I think we still have the right page, page 4, this is still Exhibit number ID 44. This is a statement. I'd like you to turn to paragraph 4. As you can see, we can read as follows: "[In English] Logistics operations declined. Food supplies were irregular. There was fighting around the Krajina which made it impossible for convoys to get through there." [Interpretation] Does this remind you of the fact that there was fighting in Krajina and that was a reason why the convoys couldn't get through?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I believe that at the time I was very well able to recall what the basis of this problem was, but at this moment -- and I did state that at the time and I will stand by that statement. At this moment I do not recall if this was actually so.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were you informed of the fact that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was preventing the fuel from reaching DutchBat and more specifically in the eastern enclave, or eastern part of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the translators, could you repeat the question, please, because it was separated in two bits.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were you ever informed about the fact that the ABiH army was preventing the fuel from reaching the eastern part of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The only information I have about the stopping of convoys was that it wasn't permitted from the Bosnian Serbian headquarters, from Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Very well. As you mentioned Pale, you said today that you thought that the military authorities were there. Did you know that the Serb authorities in Pale were actually the military and -- the civilian and military?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Civilian and political authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't hear the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot recall that as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you have it now? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can actually read the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. But if there is a fault in the interpretation in French, let me know, because I mean, it's -- the idea is to have interpretation in the three languages. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: If I say to you that there was no military authority on the Serb side in Pale, could you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The only thing I know about this is that for me, Pale was the Bosnian Serb headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was it perhaps that the authorisations were fueled through the MOD or some other governmental institution?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I have no idea about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: A while ago you mentioned your encounter with a certain Mandzic between the 10th and the 11th of July. He was a commander of the Muslim forces in the northern area. Had you met Mr. Mandzic before this event or was it the first time you saw him on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: In as far as I can recall, this was the first time I met Mr. Mandzic there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You also said that in the night from the 10th to the 11th, you were taken by Muslim fighter to a headquarters which was located in a house. This house, was it an ordinary house where the headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That was an ordinary dwelling, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You couldn't distinguish it from other houses in the area?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: It looked like a normal house to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You also mention the Muslims who were armed even though they were in civilian clothes. I would like to put you a question to you. When you see an able-bodied man in the enclave in civilian clothes, you couldn't tell whether this man was a member of the army or not?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: As long as he is not wearing any military insignia, I cannot distinguish whether he is a military. If he's wearing civilian clothes with a weapon, he would to me be a civilian with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When the refugees started arriving in the compound, your compound, on the 11th of July in Potocari, isn't it fair to say that to begin with you weren't supposed to let them in the compound?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That is correct. We were not to admit the refugees to the base.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: At some point in time, nevertheless, you let these people enter the compound, is that right?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I was given permission.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Nonetheless, not all the refugees entered the compound. Why did you prevent some people from entering afterwards?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Because I was given to understand over the radio that the base was filling up with refugees, they couldn't have any more refugees. Therefore, it was pointed out that the influx of refugees into the base had to be stopped.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the compound, did you have shelters; in other words, areas which were better protected than others?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know if the shelter offered better shelter than other locations. The refugees who were brought to the factory in the base, the factory also had parts with bunkers. I have no idea if they were more solid in their construction than the former bus compound or the other space -- or the other factory space.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were the refugees put in those areas which were better protected? [Inaudible] The bunker?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I was outside much the compound and I have no idea where the refugees in the compound were sheltered. I only saw at the moment I was in the compound that many of the refugees were actually in the factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, in fact, you don't know whether all the buildings in the compound were filled with refugees and whether there was any room left for them?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That is correct. I only went to a limited part of the compound in particular the front of the compound, there, where I was reporting to my superiors.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that on that night between the 11th and 12th of July, it was a quiet night?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, in so far as you can call it calm, in comparison to the moment of the arrival of the refugees, there was one big chaos. Then in the course of the night that chaos abated somewhat. People probably got quite tired, went to sleep. There was less noise than the evening before. So if you think that this is getting calmer, then, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I certainly did not phrase my sentence properly. I was just making sure and asking you whether there had been any shelling or shooting.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: During the night, from 11 to the 12th of July, if that is what you mean, in so far as I know, there were no mortar, grenade, shootings in the direct vicinity of the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You mentioned General Mladic, who came to the base at some -- to the compound at some point in time. Is it right to say that you warned Major Franken that General Mladic was there in the compound?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The translation says that he arrived at the base. Maybe that's a mistake in the translation because that is not so. He arrived at my location and, yes, indeed, at some point in time I did inform Major Franken of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you also inform Lieutenant Colonel Karremans or was it somebody else who told him about it?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't remember speaking over the radio with Lieutenant Colonel Karremans himself. I remember speaking with Major Otter and Major Franken.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know whether Lieutenant Colonel Karremans was informed of the arrival of General Mladic in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Waiting for the translation. I reported it, and I assume that he was informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Are you saying that you have no direct knowledge of this? At the time General Mladic was in the compound, you don't know whether Colonel Karremans knew about it?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I don't know for certain that Lieutenant Colonel Karremans was aware. I was told that he -- that the news would be transmitted to him but that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you talked to General Mladic, obviously you couldn't understand what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: The words of General Mladic were interpreted for me by the interpreter accompanying him.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes. But you had no means of checking. You don't know whether your interpreter was translating everything word-for-word, what General Mladic was saying?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I can't say that for certain. I depended on his interpretation, just as I am now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'd like to briefly get back to the question of the separation of the men from their families. Is it fair to say that this separation was conducted in the presence of DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: We were indeed present at that moment, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And during the separation process, you observed no ill treatment?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Abuse of whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Ill treatment of the Muslims by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: As I indicated earlier, when the Muslim population was being chased to the buses, people were indeed chased by the Bosnian Serbs and that happened by kicking at them and yelling at them and pushing at them so if you consider that to be abuse, then, yes, I did see abuse.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit number 1D45. This is a statement which you made and gave to the Dutch army in September 1995. Turn to paragraph 4, please, second sentence. "[In English] They made it clear to him that they wished to walk among the refugees. They did so under the supervision of UN personnel. Men were then selected by them on the basis of age. The target group, possible BiH fighters, were removed from the group and made to stand to one side. He did not see what happened to these men. At the time of the selection he did not see any ill treatment." [Interpretation] This is your September 1995 statement, i.e., two months after the events. Can one say that this --

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Correct, and what I said earlier concerns [inaudible] after the refugees were being transported, what I'm describing happened when the Bosnian Serb soldiers arrived and walked through the refugees, and selected the men that way. I remember that situation. At that point, the situation was not such yet that the refugees were being transported.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that between the 12th and 13th of July, the Serb military were not in the compound?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I hear the word "compound." How do you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we show the witness Exhibit number 1D44, please? This is the statement which you gave to the OTP. Page 14, second paragraph. Sir, we can read as follows: "[In English] During the night the Serbian soldiers were not there any longer." [Interpretation] I don't know what you had in mind when you said they were not in the compound and around the compound. Can you confirm this, please?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: To me, the location of the compound is not where I was, and if that's what you're referring to, then what this states is correct. The site where I was in the course of the night, I did not see any more Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Concerning the base, do you have any indications that they were there?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, two things. I understand that you wish to address the Chamber, the Trial Chamber, at some point before we adjourn. The other thing is this: I think we should -- we are not going to finish with this witness today obviously, and -- but I wouldn't like to postpone the tendering of the exhibits until the next time when he shows up again. I would rather have the Prosecution tender its documents today and any other documents that have been made use by the Defence. So we'll require an extra two minutes, apart from what you require.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can stop now and I can stop my cross-examination if you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I'm saying is we require two minutes for tendering the documents. I don't know how much time you require yourself to address the Trial Chamber on whatever you wish to address it upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need five minutes to address the Chamber and to finish my cross-examination I would need approximately 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we stop here. Colonel, unfortunately, I was too optimistic. We haven't finished with your testimony but basically that means you will have to return. The arrangements will be coordinated by the special units that we have here. You're still testifying basically so the understanding is that there should be no approach between Prosecution and the witness between now and when he testifies again, unless there is special reason to do so, in which case you will need -- you will require our permission before doing so. Same applies to you, Colonel. You're not to discuss with anyone the subject matter of your testimony until it's all over. So I thank you. I wish you good evening and a safe journey to wherever you're going. And we'll see you again. Usher, you can escort when the interpretation is finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's do this first, Prosecution. Mr. Thayer, I don't know if I caught you on the wrong foot but are you in a position to complete the tendering process or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thanks to Ms. Stewart, I am, Your Honour. We -- we only have one exhibit, I believe, with respect to this witness. That is PIC00025, that is the familiar overhead of Potocari marked by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Any objection? None? Okay. So admitted. Now, Popovic team, Mr. Zivanovic, you made use of 1D44, 1D45, 1D50 do you wish to tender those three documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection from the Prosecution or any of the other Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay so they are so admitted. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour I made use of one aerial photograph of Potocari but I believe that will have a number from the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that will be 4DIC26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So that is also I suppose admitted and I hear no objections. So it is so admitted. Okay. Madam Fauveau, do you wish to address the Trial Chamber in open session or in private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is about tomorrow's witness but I think it can be in -- now I'm just going to refer to number 25 which is the number given to the witness. He was supposed to come further to 92 bis and the cross-examination of this witness was to be limited to the points related to the nine bodies. Now, on the 12th of October this year, we received a request by the Prosecutor asking for the witness statement to be admitted further to 92 ter. If this is the case, of course, the Defence will request to have a full cross-examination because Rule 92 ter provides that there should be cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I add one point, Your Honour? Under the new rules, Rule 92 bis(C) would in our submission be applicable and so automatically, Rule 92 ter shall apply. So we submit that the evidence, if admissible, must be admissible under Rule 92 ter rather than 92 bis, and in our submission, the restrictions on cross-examination would therefore not apply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's be precise before we -- let's try -- I need to go into the mail to see exactly what we have admitted and what we haven't because since we agreed that we will not be dealing with this witness today, I sent back or actually I took back all the papers relating to him to my Chamber so I have got absolutely nothing in front of me. I only remember the number we are going to give him. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: If I could assist, Your Honour, by the Trial Chamber's decision of 12th of September of this year, it's paragraph 66 and in particular 67 of that decision that is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but then didn't we follow -- this is the 12th September, yeah, okay. But then we followed up with the other decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic has some recollection of that, Your Honour. I'm afraid I don't have it to hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The impression but again, I apologise to everyone in the sense that not having been aware that this was going to be raised, you may have noticed me walk out with documents during the previous break. Everything related to the next witness I took back so that my secretary will organise it better for tomorrow morning, for tomorrow afternoon, so unfortunately I don't have -- my recollection is the following, Mr. Josse: It's true, if you refer to our decision of the 12th of September, you're 100 per cent correct, both you and Madam Fauveau. However, then later on, very recently, this week, we dealt with the matter of certification that was sought by General Miletic and General Gvero, and although we did not agree with the argumentation of Madam Fauveau, we did revise our previous decision in relation to the restricted cross-examination of both Koster and the next witness, and extended it to cover everything, if I remember well. But again I don't have it here. This is why I said I would need to go into my mail account here, which I don't have on, and check.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's the 17th of October decision, Your Honour, and Your Honour changed the decision in relation to Messrs. Koster and Groenewegen and also ordered that Witness 23 appear. Your Honour and the Court was silent on Witness 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's correct that's my recollection I just came in because that's my witness and I heard that this topic was being raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any way we will deal with this tomorrow as soon as we reconvene. We'll have an opportunity to take into account your submissions and we'll come back with -- yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have a brief -- some thoughts on this if we have time. It does impinge on the witness tomorrow because he's been told by me that he will be testifying just on the limited basis of the witnesses in Potocari. I respectfully completely disagree with the Defence submission. It's being raised very late. All that's changed here are three letters in italic, bis or ter. Mr. Josse is correct that under 92 bis(C) now, the 92 ter controls if a witness is brought for cross. That means that our motion, our filing, in effect, was meaningless because 92 ter would cover it any way. And I'll be very brief because you want to finish, but it's just inconceivable to me that in creating 92 ter, the intent in the Plenary was to take away the inherent discretion that every court has to control the scope of Prosecution. The Court's ordered that he brought for 92 bis based on the sound reasoning in that decision. Now that it's 92 ter it makes so difference. That's my very short points. I would have some more and there is precedents for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls, we are not going to argue this, Madam Fauveau, today, because it's not my intention to keep anybody much longer here. We'll be discussing this amongst ourselves tomorrow in the morning before we reconvene for the sitting in the afternoon. I don't think we are in a position to anticipate anything because we need to discuss obviously, so we'll see. We'll see tomorrow morning. So I thank you so much. Have a nice evening. And we'll reconvene tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 27th day of October, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.
